raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Maintenance requests can share a fixed manual while only the sensor observation
changes. Add a small client showing how to place that manual first, preserve its
exact token prefix, and inspect SGLang's existing cache reuse through complete
OpenAI-compatible streaming responses.

## Modifications

```text
fixed manual + changing observation -> /v1/completions -> text + cache usage
```

The example reports first-text and full-response latency, completion-token counts,
cache hits and output checks. It distinguishes unknown cache usage from zero,
rejects incomplete streams, and keeps incorrect model outputs. Request failures
are written to JSONL and return a nonzero exit code. Outer Markdown fences can be
normalized for schema checks; raw text and raw JSON validity remain separate.

Scope: four files (client, short guide, runtime README link, registered CPU unit
tests). No serving, scheduler or kernel changes. This demonstrates existing cache
behavior; it does not introduce a new cache algorithm or claim a speedup from
this patch. `bench_serving` remains the tool for throughput benchmarks.

## Accuracy Tests

Clean-environment validation on 2026-10-19:

- Example head `8f9db9c5103cf275e6c77f431db7f59448aaebba`, based on main
  `8e37c6cf372427af12e8ed2c1d56b6196ea681d7`; serving uses the separate CPU
  startup fix in #44064 at `ada983f1d0513e05cb8af772f030068ad8499c42`.
- All 56 applicable direct requirements from that source's CPU manifest and
  their transitive dependencies were installed in a fresh isolated Linux venv.
  Every direct requirement matches, and `python -m pip check` passes.
  Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.14.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0, Triton 3.8.0,
  XGrammar 0.2.7; AVX2, no AVX-512/AMX/GPU or installed `sgl_kernel`.
- All 11 unchanged client tests pass using `CustomTestCase`; registered in
  `base-a-test-cpu`, with no server or model download required for the tests.
  Run: `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python test/registered/unit/examples/test_cpu_prefix_reuse.py -f`.
- The unchanged example completed three cache-on and three cache-off
  Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct FP32 requests against the installed PR source,
  without a `PYTHONPATH` override. Normalized schema and diagnosis checks pass
  6/6. Raw JSON validity is 0/6 because outputs contain Markdown fences; the
  example preserves those outputs and reports the distinction.
- All applicable configured pre-commit checks previously passed for the four
  changed files; submitted code and tests are unchanged by this validation.

The paired input hashes match, with cache hits shown below. This is a functional
smoke, not a performance benchmark.

| Cache | Requests completed | Cached tokens per request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| on | 3/3 | 0, 385, 378 |
| off | 3/3 | 0, 0, 0 |

Unpatched base needs its optional CPU kernel imports addressed before serving on
this AVX2 environment; the guide links #44064. This PR only adds the example,
guide and tests. Optimized AMX execution and upstream CI remain unverified.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The short workload demonstrates full-response measurement and cache usage; it
does not establish a performance improvement. Use `bench_serving` for throughput.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit checks and code style checks pass.
- [x] 11 focused client tests added, registered and run locally.
- [x] CPU setup, output interpretation and cache-on/off comparison documented.
- [x] Client tests and six complete requests rerun with the exact CPU dependency manifest in a fresh isolated venv.
- [ ] Upstream CI remains pending; no performance benchmark is claimed.

@@ -0,0 +1,96 @@
+# CPU prefix reuse with complete maintenance responses
+
+Put the shared maintenance manual before the changing observation:
+
+```text
+shared manual + current observation -> /v1/completions -> full text + cache usage
+```
+
+This example sends three synthetic tickets and records complete model text, HTTP time to
+first text, full-response time, reported cache hits and simple format/label checks.
+It does not send commands to hardware. Incorrect outputs remain in the JSONL file.
+An optional outer Markdown fence is normalized for schema/label checks; the raw
+text is preserved and `raw_json_valid` separately reports whether it was unfenced
+JSON. No fields or labels are repaired. Chat serialization explicitly requests
+`return_dict=False` so the prompt contains integer token IDs across tokenizer API
+versions, rather than a `BatchEncoding` object.
+
+The client is CPU independent. The following fallback launch was verified on
+SGLang v0.5.13 and main `8e37c6cf` with the
+[optional CPU startup fix](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44064),
+Linux x86-64 with AVX2 and no AMX, CPU-only Torch, and
+Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct. It uses FP32 `torch_native` attention; it is not a
+benchmark of optimized Xeon AMX or W8A8 kernels. Prepare a server using the
+[CPU installation guide](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/hardware-platforms/cpu_server).
+The launch below assumes the model and its tokenizer are already downloaded.
+
+For the verified AVX2 fallback, use the `v0.5.13` CPU dependency manifest
+(`python/pyproject_cpu.toml`) with Python 3.12 and the PyTorch CPU wheel index
+(`https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`). The tested versions are Torch
+`2.12.0+cpu`, Transformers `5.8.1` and httpx `0.28.1`. This native FP32 path did
+not require the optimized CPU extension. On an unpatched main, optional CPU
+kernel imports can still require `sgl_kernel` during startup; the linked fix
+restores native serving without that extension. The optimized x86 CPU extension
+targets AVX-512/AMX and should be installed on supported hardware following the
+guide. AOT-only features still require it; this example uses ordinary FP32
+serving and radix cache.
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1
+export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""
+export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4
+export MKL_NUM_THREADS=4
+# Choose four available CPUs on your host; check taskset -pc $$ first.
+export SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0,2,4,6
+taskset -c 0,2,4,6 python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path /path/to/pinned-model \
+  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct \
+  --device cpu --dtype float32 --attention-backend torch_native \
+  --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-cuda-graph --tp 1 \
+  --max-running-requests 1 --max-total-tokens 4096 --context-length 2048 \
+  --enable-cache-report --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
+```
+
+After startup warmup finishes (`The server is fired up and ready to roll!`):
+
+```bash
+python examples/runtime/cpu_prefix_reuse.py \
+  --model-path /path/to/the-same-pinned-model \
+  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct \
+  --cache-report-enabled --output /tmp/cpu-prefix-on.jsonl
+```
+
+Each stdout/JSONL row includes `status`, `manual_prefix_tokens`, `cached_tokens`,
+`ttft_s`, `full_s`, `completion_tokens`, `text` and output checks. Expect a cold
+first request followed by cache hits; the cache-off run should report zeros.
+Request failures are retained with `status="error"` and cause exit code 1.
+Model format or prediction errors remain evaluation results and do not change
+the exit code.
+
+For a cache-off comparison, stop that server and start a fresh one with identical
+options plus `--disable-radix-cache`. Rerun the client with a different output path.
+Keep the tokenizer/model revision, input hashes, affinity and output limit equal.
+Compare the first cold request separately from the subsequent two requests.
+This short example demonstrates functionality; repeated orders and more tickets
+are needed for a performance conclusion. Full-response time includes generated
+work, so check completion-token counts and prediction quality alongside latency.
+
+Cache reporting must be enabled on the server before passing
+`--cache-report-enabled` to the client. In the tested OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
+final usage can omit `prompt_tokens_details` when a hit is zero; this is recorded
+as zero only under that explicit flag. Without it, a missing hit remains `null`.
+An absent final usage with reporting enabled, an invalid hit count, or a truncated
+stream is an error. Shared-prefix length comes from the final serialized token IDs,
+not the manual's character count. A reported hit can include additional common
+tokens beyond the manual. Changing the early prompt prevents reuse.
+
+Hardware and software versions should accompany any benchmark result. The
+fallback is deliberately small and serial and does not imply hard real-time
+control, general industrial diagnostic accuracy, or MCU model deployment.
+
+Client regression tests require no server or model weights and are registered
+in the CPU CI suite:
+
+```bash
+python test/registered/unit/examples/test_cpu_prefix_reuse.py -f
+```

+"""Measure complete responses to synthetic maintenance tickets sharing a manual.
+
+Run against a fresh SGLang server launched with --enable-cache-report.
+This example uses exact tokenizer-produced IDs and reports errors alongside latency.
+See CPU_PREFIX_REUSE.md for CPU launch options and the cache-off comparison.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import httpx
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+MANUAL = """You are a maintenance assistant for a synthetic cooling station.
+Classify CURRENT, not HISTORY, using the first matching rule:
+1. sensor_valid=false: diagnosis=sensor_fault, action=CHECK_SENSOR.
+2. temperature_c>=60 and fan_rpm<500: diagnosis=cooling_fault, action=FAN_ON.
+3. load>=90: diagnosis=load_rise, action=KEEP.
+4. Otherwise: diagnosis=normal, action=KEEP.
+Return a complete JSON object with three string fields: diagnosis, action, reason.
+The reason must be a short explanation. No Markdown or extra fields.
+
+Equipment knowledge: the fan cools the motor enclosure. fan_rpm describes the
+cooling fan, rather than the motor shaft. A zero fan speed during a cool idle
+period does not alone imply a cooling fault. sensor_valid comes from the local
+input check; its value is authoritative even if the temperature appears normal.
+History is context only: a previous fault does not override a recovered current
+sample, and a previous valid probe does not repair a currently invalid one.
+
+Maintenance procedures: for a sensor fault, inspect the temperature-probe
+connection and obtain a valid sample before diagnosing the cooling system.
+For a cooling fault, keep local protective cooling enabled and inspect fan
+obstruction and the cooling path. For a high load, retain local controls and
+inspect the process load trend. For normal operation, continue monitoring.
+
+Action boundaries: KEEP does not clear an alarm or force cooling off. FAN_ON
+requests cooling only. CHECK_SENSOR requests inspection. Local MCU protection
+continues independently; this assistant is not a safety controller. A gateway
+must validate any action before transmitting it to a device. The example only
+generates text and never controls physical equipment.
+"""
+
+CASES = [
+    (
+        {"sensor_valid": True, "temperature_c": 45, "fan_rpm": 1000, "load": 30},
+        "normal",
+    ),
+    (
+        {"sensor_valid": True, "temperature_c": 75, "fan_rpm": 200, "load": 50},
+        "cooling_fault",
+    ),
+    (
+        {"sensor_valid": False, "temperature_c": -40, "fan_rpm": 1000, "load": 30},
+        "sensor_fault",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+def stream_completion(client, url, payload, cache_report_enabled):
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    first = None
+    texts = []
+    usage = None
+    done = False
+    with client.stream("POST", url, json=payload) as response:
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        lines = []
+        for line in response.iter_lines():
+            if line.startswith("data:"):
+                lines.append(line[5:].lstrip())
+                if sum(map(len, lines)) > 65536:
+                    raise ValueError("oversized SSE event")
+                continue
+            if line or not lines:
+                continue
+            event = "\n".join(lines)
+            lines.clear()
+            if event == "[DONE]":
+                done = True
+                break
+            chunk = json.loads(event)
+            if "error" in chunk:
+                raise ValueError(f"backend error: {chunk['error']}")
+            for choice in chunk.get("choices", []):
+                text = choice.get("text", "")
+                if text:
+                    if first is None:
+                        first = time.perf_counter() - started
+                    texts.append(text)
+            if chunk.get("usage"):
+                usage = chunk["usage"]
+    if not done or first is None:
+        raise ValueError("incomplete token-bearing response")
+    cached = ((usage or {}).get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens")
+    if cache_report_enabled:
+        if usage is None:
+            raise ValueError("cache reporting was enabled but final usage is missing")
+        # The tested SGLang server omits prompt_tokens_details for a zero hit.
+        cached = 0 if cached is None else cached
+    if cached is not None and (
+        type(cached) is not int or not 0 <= cached <= len(payload["prompt"])
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid cached-token count")
+    return {
+        "text": "".join(texts),
+        "ttft_s": first,
+        "full_s": time.perf_counter() - started,
+        "cached_tokens": cached,
+        "completion_tokens": (usage or {}).get("completion_tokens"),
+    }
+
+
+def parse_output(text):
+    """Normalize an outer Markdown fence, while retaining raw JSON validity."""
+    raw_json = True
+    try:
+        value = json.loads(text)
+    except json.JSONDecodeError:
+        raw_json = False
+        stripped = text.strip()
+        if not (stripped.startswith("```") and stripped.endswith("```")):
+            raise
+        first_line, separator, body = stripped.partition("\n")
+        if not separator or first_line not in {"```", "```json"}:
+            raise ValueError("unsupported output wrapper")
+        value = json.loads(body[:-3].strip())
+    if not (
+        isinstance(value, dict)
+        and set(value) == {"diagnosis", "action", "reason"}
+        and all(isinstance(v, str) for v in value.values())
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("output does not match the three-string schema")
+    return value, raw_json
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="server's served-model-name")
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1")
+    parser.add_argument("--cache-report-enabled", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    failed = False
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, local_files_only=True)
+    prefix = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+        [{"role": "system", "content": MANUAL}],
+        tokenize=True,
+        add_generation_prompt=False,
+        return_dict=False,
+    )
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with (
+        args.output.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as output,
+        httpx.Client(timeout=180, trust_env=False) as client,
+    ):
+        for index, (current, expected) in enumerate(CASES):
+            messages = [
+                {"role": "system", "content": MANUAL},
+                {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps({"CURRENT": current})},
+            ]
+            ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+                messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=False
+            )
+            if ids[: len(prefix)] != prefix:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "system prefix is not exact in the final serialization"
+                )
+            row = {
+                "index": index,
+                "input_tokens": len(ids),
+                "manual_prefix_tokens": len(prefix),
+                "input_sha256": hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(ids).encode()).hexdigest(),
+                "expected": expected,
+                "format_valid": False,
+                "raw_json_valid": False,
+                "diagnosis_correct": False,
+            }
+            try:
+                result = stream_completion(
+                    client,
+                    args.base_url.rstrip("/") + "/completions",
+                    {
+                        "model": args.model,
+                        "prompt": ids,
+                        "max_tokens": 96,
+                        "temperature": 0,
+                        "stream": True,
+                        "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
+                    },
+                    args.cache_report_enabled,
+                )
+                row.update(result, status="completed")
+                try:
+                    value, raw_json = parse_output(result["text"])
+                    row.update(
+                        format_valid=True,
+                        raw_json_valid=raw_json,
+                        diagnosis_correct=value["diagnosis"] == expected,
+                    )
+                except (ValueError, TypeError):
+                    pass
+            except (ValueError, httpx.HTTPError) as error:
+                failed = True
+                row.update(status="error", error=str(error))
+            line = json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False)
+            output.write(line + "\n")
+            output.flush()
+            print(line, flush=True)
+    return int(failed)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Client contract tests using real httpx response streams, without model weights."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import httpx
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+    "cpu_prefix_example",
+    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "examples/runtime/cpu_prefix_reuse.py",
+)
+example = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+spec.loader.exec_module(example)
+
+
+class TestCPUPrefixReuse(CustomTestCase):
+    def run_cli(self, tokenizer, **completion):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            output = Path(directory) / "completed.jsonl"
+            with (
+                patch(
+                    "sys.argv",
+                    [
+                        "example",
+                        "--model-path",
+                        "local",
+                        "--model",
+                        "test",
+                        "--output",
+                        str(output),
+                    ],
+                ),
+                patch.object(
+                    example.AutoTokenizer, "from_pretrained", return_value=tokenizer
+                ),
+                patch.object(example, "stream_completion", **completion),
+                patch("builtins.print"),
+            ):
+                code = example.main()
+            rows = [json.loads(line) for line in output.read_text().splitlines()]
+        return code, rows
+
+    def test_cli_serializes_ids_across_tokenizer_return_types(self):
+        # Transformers can return a mapping unless return_dict=False is explicit.
+        tokenizer = MagicMock()
+        tokenizer.apply_chat_template.side_effect = lambda *args, **kwargs: (
+            [1, 2] if kwargs.get("return_dict") is False else {"input_ids": [1, 2]}
+        )
+        result = {"text": '{"diagnosis":"normal","action":"KEEP","reason":"ok"}'}
+        code, rows = self.run_cli(tokenizer, return_value=result)
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(len(rows), len(example.CASES))
+        self.assertTrue(all(row["status"] == "completed" for row in rows))
+        self.assertTrue(all(row["input_tokens"] == 2 for row in rows))
+
+    def test_cli_retains_request_errors_and_returns_failure(self):
+        tokenizer = MagicMock()
+        tokenizer.apply_chat_template.return_value = [1, 2]
+        code, rows = self.run_cli(
+            tokenizer, side_effect=ValueError("backend unavailable")
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(len(rows), len(example.CASES))
+        self.assertTrue(all(row["status"] == "error" for row in rows))
+        self.assertTrue(all(row["error"] == "backend unavailable" for row in rows))
+
+    def test_fences_do_not_repair_wrong_labels(self):
+        text = '```json\n{"diagnosis":"wrong", "action":"KEEP", "reason":"x"}\n```'
+        value, raw = example.parse_output(text)
+        self.assertFalse(raw)
+        self.assertEqual(value["diagnosis"], "wrong")
+
+    def test_schema_and_extra_commentary_rejected(self):
+        for text in (
+            '{"diagnosis":"normal"}',
+            '```json\n{"diagnosis":"normal","action":"KEEP","reason":"x","extra":1}\n```',
+            'comment\n{"diagnosis":"normal","action":"KEEP","reason":"x"}',
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(text=text), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                example.parse_output(text)
+
+    def run_stream(self, usage, *, report=True, done=True, error=False):
+        chunks = [{"choices": [{"text": ""}]}, {"choices": [{"text": "hello"}]}]
+        if error:
+            chunks.append({"error": {"message": "backend failure"}})
+        if usage is not None:
+            chunks.append({"choices": [], "usage": usage})
+        wire = ": heartbeat\n\n" + "".join(
+            "data: " + json.dumps(c) + "\n\n" for c in chunks
+        )
+        if done:
+            wire += "data: [DONE]\n\n"
+        client = httpx.Client(
+            transport=httpx.MockTransport(
+                lambda request: httpx.Response(200, text=wire)
+            )
+        )
+        with client:
+            return example.stream_completion(
+                client,
+                "http://test/completions",
+                {"prompt": list(range(10)), "max_tokens": 96},
+                report,
+            )
+
